## Introduction

In this report we explore a dataset of movies taken from the Internet Movie Database (IMDb). The goal of this analysis is to see if there is a relationship between movie budgets, revenues and ratings.

The analysis has three parts:

1\. We first load and describe the data,

2\. We preprocess the data

3\. We visualise it.

## The Data

We use the `dplyr` package to manipulate the data and the `ggplot2` package to create plots.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

The data is stored in the file `CleanMovies.csv`, which we load into R as a data frame called `movies`.

```{r}
movies <- read.csv("CleanMovies.csv")
head(movies)
```

The dataset contains `r nrow(movies)` films and `r ncol(movies)` variables. For each film we have its `title`, the year it was released (`release_year`), its average viewer `rating` (out of 100), its `budget` and `revenue` (in millions of US dollars), whether it is in English (`EnglishLang`), and six `TRUE`/`FALSE` columns recording whether it belongs to each of the genres Action, Comedy, Drama, Family, Horror and SciFi.
